title: Y-coordinate after a stretch parallel to the y-axis
source: Theory P1-2.7 Quick check 1 (point (2, 4) on y=f(x) maps to (2, 12) on y=3f(x)); new positive scale factors and y-coordinates
stem: The point \((2, {q|int})\) lies on the graph of \(y=f(x)\). What is the \(y\)-coordinate of the image of this point on the graph of \(y={a|int}f(x)\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: A stretch of scale factor {a|int} parallel to the \(y\)-axis multiplies the \(y\)-coordinate by {a|int}, so the image has \(y\)-coordinate \({a|int}\times{q|int}={A|int}\).
steps.note: A is a q. Original a=3, q=4 gives 12.

title: X-coordinate after a stretch parallel to the x-axis
source: Theory P1-2.7 Quick check 2 (point (4, 5) on y=f(x) corresponds to (2, 5) on y=f(2x)); new even x-coordinates and integer factors
stem: The point \(({p|int}, 5)\) lies on the graph of \(y=f(x)\). The same \(y\)-value occurs on the graph of \(y=f({k|int}x)\) at \((c, 5)\). What is the value of \(c\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The graph of \(y=f({k|int}x)\) is a stretch of scale factor \(1/{k|int}\) parallel to the \(x\)-axis, so the new \(x\)-coordinate is \({p|int}/{k|int}={A|int}\).
steps.note: A is p/k. Original k=2, p=4 gives c=2.

title: Stretched y-value of a known point
source: Theory P1-2.7 Quick check 3 (the point at height 5 is stretched to height 15 when the scale factor is 3); new factors
stem: A point on the graph of \(y=f(x)\) has \(y\)-coordinate 5. After a stretch of scale factor {a|int} parallel to the \(y\)-axis, what is the new \(y\)-coordinate of this point?

title: Single stretch taking y=x squared + 2x - 5 to y=4x squared + 4x - 5

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2022), Question 4(b) only. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark. Part 4(a) is a translation, already used in package 8 (P1-2.5), and is omitted. Part (b) is independent of (a).

stem:
This question is 9709/13/M/J/22 Question 4(b), taken from the official QP.

The curve with equation \(y=x^2+2x-5\) is transformed to a curve with equation \(y=4x^2+4x-5\).

Describe fully the single transformation that has been applied.  [2]

steps.name: B
steps.text_tex: The image is obtained by replacing \(x\) with \(2x\) in \(x^2+2x-5\), so the single transformation is a stretch of scale factor \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) parallel to the \(x\)-axis (equivalently, horizontally, or with the \(y\)-axis invariant).
steps.note: Official MS 4(b): B2, 1, 0 for the three elements Stretch; x direction or horizontally or y-axis invariant; factor 1/2. Additional transformation scores B0. Independent: f(2x)=(2x)^2+2(2x)-5=4x^2+4x-5.
